title: Philip III to the Count of Añover, Lerma, 20 May 1610 (Madrid, Biblioteca Histórica Municipal, I 242,29): a partial nomenclator rebuilt from sibling letters (catalogue 1988)

steps.what: The contributor obtained images of I 242,29 and the siblings I 242,33, 42, 47, 48 and 71 from Memoria de Madrid; the images of 47 and 48 reached him by a user's contribution (his report). The project's own requests to the viewer returned 403.

Sequences of the ciphers of I 242,42, 47, 48 and 33 matched with their contemporary clear texts to give group values (66 graded C, 3 M, 5 I in the table for I 242,29); I 242,71 kept apart as a negative control (the earlier key is not transferred).

Ten lines of f. 53r read in part: Dutch factory at Pinda, Angola coast, against the truce; the king charges the count to see it remedied and report. The contributor's figures: 173 of 211 group occurrences in firm words (81.99%), 202 of 211 with an equivalence in the table (95.73%), 78 of 88 words firm.

Own parser applied to the transcription and key table of the report (all segmentations of the digit runs): 213 tokens, two not in the table as written; the output is the contributor's reading, ten lines of connected Spanish. The transcription and the sibling parallels are not checked against the manuscripts.

Control of my own, Spanish 1490-1650 quadgrams on the decode against 200 permutations of the digit values: real -4.39 per letter, best permutation -4.20: inconclusive on this short syllabic text; not relied on. The contributor's own control was not re-run.

Prior art: Tomokiyo, DECODE, Retortillo Atienza 2019 and Correia searched by the contributor; a web search here found no mention of a 1610 cipher letter to Añover about Pinda; Devos 1950 not consulted.

English translation contributed by Alberto Garvía García (PR #547, translation.md): line by line on reading.md, the same 12 bracketed holes in the same lines and order (checked by script), no claim of a complete decipherment. Two small fixes here: line 1 'it has been learned [101: report?]' put back as 'word [101: report?] has been had' so the bracketed code is not translated twice; line 5 the null 58~ restored in its place inside 'stipu-la[58~: null?]ted' with its gloss.

Issue #499 comments of 13 Nov 2026: the contributor's 211-token analytical layer and his control windows A01-D06, E01-E04 saved in contributor/; all 211 tokens have a value in key.tsv and decode to his reading letter for letter; the 74-entry graded table equals key.tsv. Dudout's independent transcription comparison (all digit strings of L01-L10 agree; L05 bo/60 doubtful) recorded. Memoria de Madrid still 403, images not seen. No open code closed; the contributor's own word count unchanged (78 of 88 words, 88.6%; the project's strict recount of 14 Nov is 77 of 89, 86.5%).

Brice Dudout's token-by-gloss alignment of the glossed letter I 243,18 (Memoria de Madrid 425791, 30 Apr 1610; issue #499, 14 Nov 2026; contributor/i243_18_dudout_alignment.txt) compared with key.tsv: 71 pairs agree, 1 does not (mel glossed or once), 24 tokens are not in the table; none of the open codes U01, 101, 114, 241, e, fo occurs, so no open code is closed. The contributor reports the same and confirms L05 bo 32 on the images. His two new zip attachments return 403 and were not seen. The alignment was not compared with the image.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 205 tokens, 68 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -1.948 per letter; random keys -3.627 (z 7.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.176 (mean -2.221, z 10.4); annealer on the real text -2.119. Verdict: pass.

Statistical check with docs/_validate.py on the contributor's 211 tokens and key.tsv (validation.tsv; the six context-only or single-parallel values left unread, the two doubtful nulls read as nothing): -1.948 per letter in the Spanish 4-gram model against -3.627 on average for 200 random keys of the same structure (best -3.001, z 7.7) and -2.176 at best for a key annealed onto the shuffled ciphertext (z 10.4). Verdict pass, on 205 tokens and 68 types, with a key that came from the sibling clear texts, not from this text. It replaces the inconclusive control of 13 Nov, which permuted digit values only.

Strict recount of the read share from reading.md, word by word: 89 words in the ten lines; 10 are marked holes (buena, aviso, puerto, otras, entablando, trato, capitulado, bien, disimulacion, persona: a context-only code, a revisable transfer with no direct parallel (fo = so, grade M), a doubtful null inside the word or the otraas anomaly) and 2 more rest on a sign the transcriptions do not settle (mando, the sign printed gel{b?}; porque in line 5, bo in one transcription and 60 in the other). 77 of 89 words sure = 86.5%. The contributor's own count is 78 of 88 words (88.6%).

Write-up as read in part by the owner's decision. Memoria de Madrid was not asked again by script (it refused on 13 and 14 Nov with an Access Denied page, a bot check, not got round). The project's only sight of the manuscript is page 2 in a browser at the catalogue sweep of 2 Nov 2026 (no copy kept; the opening groups noted then agree with line 1 of the contributor's transcription); the transcription was not compared with the image, and no image is shown. The contributor's two zip packages of 14 Nov returned 403 and were not seen.

Holes: the 10 words the reading brackets (buena U01, aviso 101, trato 241, bien 114: context-only codes; disimulacion: e = mu from context; persona: fo = so, a revisable transfer, grade M, no direct parallel in key.tsv; puerto, entablando, capitulado: a doubtful null 28~ or 58~ inside the word; otras: the otraas anomaly) and 2 words on a sign the transcriptions do not settle (mando, gel{b?}; porque in line 5, bo or 60). The contributor's own figure is 78 of 88 words = 0.886 (his looser ones: 173 of 211 group occurrences in firm words, 202 of 211 with a table equivalence).
outcome.notes: Written up as read in part on 14 Nov 2026 (owner's decision). Ten lines of f. 53r read in part from a key rebuilt from sibling letters; 77 of 89 words sure. The open codes are still workable from the unglossed and further glossed letters of the series, which belong to catalogue 1988.

texts.label: Philip III to the Count of Añover, 20 May 1610 (I 242,29): the ten transcribed lines
texts.summary: Philip III learns that Dutchmen have gone to set up a factory at Pinda on the coast of Angola, against the truce, and charges the Count of Añover to remedy it without sending anyone to the Islands, and to report.

reading_review.note: decryption.txt and reading.md read as Spanish sentences against translation.md: the ten lines are one connected royal order (news of the Dutch at Pinda; the charge to remedy it; no person to be sent to the Islands; report back) and every clause holds. 12 of 89 words are holes (10 bracketed in the reading, 2 on an unsettled sign); they are scattered, and the sense of each is narrow, which is why grade A. Not compared with the manuscript.

texts.note: Words 89; sure 77 (0.865). The 12 holes are listed in outcome.fraction_read_source.

prior.where: No reading of I 242,29 known: the contributor searched Tomokiyo, DECODE, Retortillo Atienza 2019 and the Correia thesis; a web search here found none. Devos 1950 not consulted.

human: Alberto Garvía García directed the work and posted it; the transcription, matching with the sibling clear texts and the key table were prepared with ChatGPT/Codex (his statement). No independent palaeographic check. This project checked the report and re-derived the reading from his transcription and key table with its own parser; the manuscripts could not be fetched.
